In [[mathematics]], specifically [[Group theory#Finite group theory|finite group theory]], a '''p-group of symplectic type''' is a [[p-group|''p''-group]] such that all [[characteristic subgroup|characteristic]] [[abelian group|abelian]] [[subgroup]]s are [[cyclic group|cyclic]].

According to {{harvtxt|Thompson|1968|loc=p.386}}, the ''p''-groups of symplectic type were classified by P. Hall in unpublished lecture notes, who showed that they are all a central product of an [[extraspecial group]] with a group that is cyclic, [[dihedral group|dihedral]], quasidihedral, or quaternion. {{harvtxt|Gorenstein|1980|loc=5.4.9}} gives a [[mathematical proof|proof]] of this result.

The '''width''' ''n'' of a group ''G'' of symplectic type is the largest integer ''n'' such that the group contains an extraspecial subgroup ''H'' of [[order (group theory)|order]] ''p''<sup>1+2''n''</sup> such that ''G'' = ''H''.''C''<sub>''G''</sub>(''H''), or 0 if ''G'' contains no such subgroup.

Groups of symplectic type appear in [[centralizer]]s of involutions of [[groups of GF(2)-type]].
